text:
Mike: Hey team — Azure marketplace deal with Contoso. Procurement is asking for clarity on invoice cadence and which vendor tax ID will appear on the invoice before they sign the PO. Who can confirm how Azure marketplace invoices get issued and whether we can map to a different billing entity?

Jenna: Azure marketplace settlements are handled by Microsoft — invoices to buyers are generated by MSFT and payouts to us follow their settlement window (typically 30–60 days, sometimes up to 90 depending on the marketplace schedule). We can't force MSFT to invoice immediately.

Jenna: Options: 1) Use a Private Offer (can be routed to invoice directly to buyer / our legal entity) but that requires setting up with MSFT and ~7–14 business days. 2) For a fast POC, customer pays by CC and we invoice/credit later on conversion.

Jenna: Vendor info we can provide (send as attachments):
```
Legal name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
EIN / TaxID: 12-3456789
Billing address: 123 Redwood Way, SF, CA 94107
W-9 available on request
```

Arjun: Quick security check — invoices do NOT contain customer prompt data or model outputs, just line items, amounts, tax info and PO# if provided. No PII/secret data on invoices. Also flag: if buyer is EU, procurement will ask about VAT number and reverse-charge handling.

Becca: Procurement at Contoso says they require invoice lines to match the SOW and want the invoice issued to "Contoso Corp — AP Dept" with their PO. For marketplace flows we need to ensure the PO number passes through MSFT; sometimes that mapping gets lost. If they insist on direct Redwood invoice, we'll need a Private Offer or to move off-marketplace.

Mike: OK. What's the Deal Desk process to request a carve-out so we can invoice directly (or have MSFT map to our vendor tax id)? Timeline?

Jenna: Deal Desk: open a ticket with the following: summary, customer, proposed rate card and commit, requested billing entity override, and attach W-9 and SOW. There's a template in Confluence: https://redwood.internal/deals/templates (link). Expect 1–3 business days for initial review, longer if legal needs to redline.

ProcurementBot: Procurement checklist (auto):
- Vendor legal name + W-9 or EU VAT certificate
- Billing contact email
- PO number format
- TaxID/VAT mapping
- SOW / line item breakdown
Upload portal: https://procurement.contoso/upload 

Becca: For this POC I can draft an SOW that splits line items (30% infra / 70% service) so their AP can match. But Deal Desk must approve any discount/commit carve-out for marketplace pricing.

Mike: Action items: Jenna — send vendor docs & W-9 to Contoso and attach to Deal Desk ticket; Becca — share a SOW line-item draft by noon tomorrow; Arjun — confirm in writing that invoice content is limited (no customer data). I'll open the Deal Desk ticket and tag legal. ETA EOD tomorrow for first pass? :eyes:

Jenna: Sending W-9 + vendor sheet to Contoso now, cc'ing AP contact. :white_check_mark:

Becca: SOW outline will be in my drive by 12pm. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Arjun: Security confirms — invoice only contains generic line items, no prompts/outputs. Good to go. :+1:

Mike: If Deal Desk can't get MSFT to map PO/taxid, fallback: run POC on CC and convert to PO on commit. Not ideal but shortest path. I’ll update thread once Deal Desk responds.

Jenna: Noted. I'll also include the note about Azure settlement lag so Contoso understands timing for revenue recognition. :memo:

Becca: Thanks — looping legal if we need a Private Offer.

Mike: Thanks everyone. Keeping this channel for updates. :thumbsup:
